citation: Melander & Henderson, 'No. 51. Residence of Mahlon D. Ogden, Esq.', stereograph, Views of Chicago Ruins, Great Fire of October 1871 (Aurora, Ill.: Melander & Henderson, 1871). Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-57071 (cph 3b04902).
author: Melander & Henderson, photographers and publishers (18 Fox Street, Aurora, Illinois; the card's mount)
describes_date: 1871, just after the fire of 8-9 October
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. The left half of the card is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3689/loc_3b04902_ogden_house_left.jpg.
locator: The left half of the card: the Ogden house behind the elms of its grounds, its front and veranda to the camera; the rubble of a burnt brick house and an iron fence in the foreground.
rights_note: The Library of Congress: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph published in 1871.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-20 (T-3689) from the Library's TIFF of the whole card (1536 x 798 px, tile.loc.gov service/pnp/cph/3b00000/3b04000/3b04902); the left half cropped and committed at 620 x 650 px, sha256 6dde084c42c251a8f2e20eca38daf0db82fbd5c59124b07be7d0eb32f09be0b8.
note: The house that survived the fire in the middle of the burnt North Side. Small, soft and half hidden by trees; monochrome.
what_it_supplies: the house's storeys, front, veranda, cornice and roof
that it stood after the fire among its trees
